quote: A solvability criterion for finite groups and some consequences. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences U.S.A., 48(6): 968–970 (1962)
posed_by: Walter Feit and John Griggs Thompson
note: The Feit-Thompson conjecture was first posed in 1962 in their landmark paper on solvability criteria for finite groups. It asserts that for all distinct prime numbers p and q, (p^q - 1)/(p - 1) does not divide (q^p - 1)/(q - 1). The conjecture remains open and was originally conceived in connection with their proof of the Feit-Thompson theorem.
